reports.title: Manchester United PLC Reports First Quarter Fiscal 2027 Results

guidance.heading: Outlook
section: For fiscal 2027, the Company reiterates its full year revenue guidance of £740 million to £760 million and adjusted EBITDA guidance of £205 million to £225 million. The club remains committed to, and in compliance with, both the Premier League’s Sustainability and Systemic Resilience Rules and Squad Cost Ratio and UEFA’s Club Licensing and Financial Sustainability Regulations.

Phasing of Premier League games | Quarter 1 | Quarter 2 | Quarter 3 | Quarter 4 | Total
2026/27 season* | 5 | 13 | 12 | 8 | 38
2025/26 season | 6 | 13 | 12 | 7 | 38
2024/25 season | 6 | 13 | 10 | 9 | 38

desk.headline: Revenue up 4.1% to £146.1m, below estimates; loss widens to £18.1m; full-year guidance reaffirmed
results: Revenue rose 4.1% to £146.1m, led by a 17.7% jump in broadcasting income from the return to the Champions League.
Commercial revenue was flat at £84.1m: sponsorship fell 3% on a smaller pre-season tour, while retail and licensing grew 3.5%.
Adjusted EBITDA edged up to £27.5m, but wages rose 8.6% to £79.9m (54.7% of revenue).
The operating result swung to a £3.0m loss from a £13.0m profit as profit on player sales fell to £20.7m from £45.0m; net loss widened to £18.1m.
Cash fell to £55.5m; the club drew a net £90m on its revolving facility and long-term US dollar debt stands at $775m after a June refinancing.

guidance.summary: The club kept its fiscal 2027 targets of £740–760m revenue and £205–225m adjusted EBITDA. No specific consensus figure for the full year was found.

watch: Results on the pitch under new head coach Mauricio Pochettino and progress in the Champions League league stage.
Q2 carries 13 Premier League games versus 5 in Q1, which should lift broadcasting and matchday income.
Debt and cash: revolving facility drawings of £200m and spending on player registrations.
